scope: Two 64-step arms - the published read-out and the same read-out centred inside the head before the objective sees it - captured in one catalogue and scored read-only at the standing 0.0 boundary and over the standing 81-point grid. The option is structural: no label, no threshold, no fitted parameter, no prevalence, and the spread is untouched so relative cell structure is unchanged. 0 is exactly the published function. No threshold change, no population change and no real-image, complete-state or quality claim.

mechanism.name: structurally-centred-read
mechanism.definition: L - mean(L[:, :visible_rows]) per board, applied inside the head before the objective or any scorer sees the tensor
mechanism.where: model head, before the loss and before every consumer
mechanism.statistic: the board's own visible-cell mean; spawn rows are scored by it and never enter it
mechanism.spread: untouched, unlike occupancy_normalise, so relative cell structure is unchanged
mechanism.alignment_invariance: centre(L + c) == centre(L) for any constant c
mechanism.unknown_cells: cells outside the visible window never enter the mean
mechanism.identity_at_zero: occupancy_centre 0 is exactly the published function
mechanism.supersedes: nothing: it is an option on the read, refused beside every supervision term, the normalised output and every read-moving lever
mechanism.failure_mode: the mean of all cells is not the F1-optimal level on a 12%-occupied population, so centring can overshoot below zero

training_occupancy.reading: the occupancy loss the arm paid; this arm adds no term of its own, so there is no separate charge to report - the structural option removes the level instead of charging it

aliasing_guard.rule: a structural option changes the read globally, so the block proves it measured its own checkpoint: each sweep's weights equal its own study's checkpoint, the arms' weights differ, the previous block's checkpoint is excluded by name, and the configs differ in exactly the declared field

reference.role: reference-only: the M13 midpoint anchor, the M12 dense hinge, the M11 quantile anchor, the M10 extremal anchor and the M9 hinge, each measured in its own catalogue and none re-measured or re-verdicted here

reading_text: Removing the read's additive mode does not put the plain-binary boundary above control's, so the level was not the obstacle after all and the operating point is bounded by the read's cell-level errors rather than by its scale or its supervision.
secondary_text: Deciding AUC with the standing -0.02 tolerance. Removing an additive mode cannot destroy separation by itself, so a ranking loss here would be the training's response to a read whose level is fixed rather than the transform's own doing - and it is reported as the measured price.
